28.description: The committee recommends advisory committees can approve spending under $2,000 within their mandate, but higher amounts or unclear items need Standing Policy Committee approval.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Councillor asked if report should be shared with affected committees.
City Council advisory committees
Administration directed to review committee mandates and engage them.

29.description: Saskatoon's Governance and Priorities Committee upheld the denial for the Saskatoon Iranian Cultural Association to fly the 1979 flag of Iran at City Hall, maintaining the policy against foreign flags.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block stated the city's role is to serve all residents
The Iranian community in Saskatoon, numbering over 3,000, sought a gesture of solidarity.
Pooyan Arab appealed, stating the flag is a cultural symbol of a people, not a country.

24.description: The committee recommends approving criteria for a new priority-based budgeting system, which would provide more program information for 2027 budget decisions.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block questioned how administrative subjectivity would make the process more transparent.
Programs will be evaluated on delivering value to residents or businesses.
Councillor Pierce questioned the low 10% weighting for legally mandated services.
Administration did not estimate the extra hours required for staff to implement PBB.
Councillor Davies would not support the new process, fearing wasted effort and subjectivity.
Criteria include addressing underserved populations and advancing the city's equity commitments.
Administration stated no additional FTEs or resources are anticipated for PBB.

26.description: The committee recommends endorsing a National Urban Park vision, governance, and initial boundary, led by Meewasin and Parks Canada, pending federal funding.

chips.text: Recommended
Meewasin Valley Authority and Parks Canada will lead the park.
Saskatoon's park model is unique with local partners leading operations.
What happens to Swale areas excluded by the provisional boundary was unclear.
Public delegates and letters raised concerns about reduced Swale protection.
Park vision includes cultural spaces for Indigenous teaching and revitalization.
Concerns raised that reduced boundaries would harm rare plant habitat and ecological buffers.
Administration promised future boundary expansions for Swale areas.

31.description: The Integrity Commissioner's 2025 annual report reflects on her four-year term, expressing confidence in the complaint process.

chips.text: Approved
Commissioner Angela Kruk handled over 50 complaints across municipalities in four years.
Council members and the public are affected by the code of ethics complaint process.

25.description: Saskatoon Council reviewed proposed provincial amendments to The Cities Act, including new provisions for appointing an Indigenous advisor and clarifying council member obligations.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block questioned the distinction between an Indigenous advisor and a council member.
Indigenous advisors will not be voting council members or count for quorum.

27.description: Saskatoon is moving forward with plans for Indigenous cultural spaces, guided by community input, to support culture, ceremony, and wellness within the city.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block questioned the need for city spaces given Wanuskewin
Key questions remain about site locations, governance
Elders and youth emphasize cultural spaces are essential for identity, healing
Project aims to address cultural disconnection, addiction, and wellness for Indigenous residents.
City staff committed to returning to Council for future decisions or approvals on the project.

30.description: The Governance and Priorities Committee recommends City Council appoint a proxy for the Remai Modern's Annual General Meeting on April 28, 2026.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Mayor Block, Councillor Dubois, or Councillor Ford would serve as proxy.
